result.summary: Adds a Sock::ShutdownSend() wrapper and uses it in the HTTP server so that after a parse error (malformed header or oversized body) the server flushes the 400/413 reply, half-closes only the write side, drains remaining client input until EOF or a 1s fallback timeout, and only then tears down the connection. This avoids the current behavior of closing immediately, which on Windows can trigger a TCP RST that discards the queued error reply before the client reads it.
result.problem: On Windows, closing a socket with unread inbound data can send a TCP RST that discards a just-queued reply, so clients rejected for a bad or oversized HTTP request never see the 400/413 response and instead see a connection reset; this also causes an intermittent CI failure (#35632) in interface_http.py.

result.card: This draft PR changes how the Bitcoin Core HTTP server closes connections after a parse error (bad header, oversized body): instead of closing immediately, it flushes the 400/413 reply, half-closes the write side via a new Sock::ShutdownSend(), and drains remaining client input until EOF or a 1s timeout. The problem is real: on Windows, closing with unread data can trigger a TCP RST that discards the queued error reply before the client reads it, which also causes an intermittent CI flake tracked in #35632. Four reviewers gave concept ACKs, but pinheadmz is not convinced by the specific mechanism and proposed a simpler approach once #35735 (now merged) lands; hodlinator has an open question about the shutdown ordering and just offered a rebase suggestion. The PR is currently draft, marked needs rebase, and conflicts with the newly opened #35829, so the present diff is expected to change before it merits full review. No hard dependency blocks it now that #35735 has merged, but a rebase and possibly a design change are pending.
